summary: The read-only allowlist `get` (Pulse room admission and the app contact detail) reads the persisted openclaw.json instead of spawning `openclaw gateway call config.get`. The file gets the same checks as the native Pulse room reader (regular file, owned by the runtime user, at most 2 MiB). Mutations keep the live Gateway config and its hash for compare-and-swap.
reason: Amine 29/10: « go lecture en mémoire aussi ». S24 profile: 2.0 of 2.05 s of one `allowlist get` is the `openclaw gateway call` CLI spawn; Python and the contact reads take 50 ms. On the S24 the persisted file and config.get give identical rows for all 5 contacts (rows 22 ms vs 2.41 s). config.patch writes the same file, so a revocation is visible to the next read.

tests.evidence: 49/49: get makes no Gateway call, equals the live find(), sees a persisted revocation at once, refuses a symlinked or oversized config.

capabilities.reason: Same contact read; no new action or field.

architecture.reason: Same owner and IPC; the read uses the file the native room reader already trusts. No cache, store or daemon.

limitations: `list` and every mutation still read the live Gateway config.
A hand edit of openclaw.json that the Gateway has not reloaded is what this read sees; config.patch keeps both in step.
rollback: Revert this commit and redeploy the core.
